comparator.route: Balanced literature, linguistics and global-culture elective route
comparator.sourceNotes: The September 2026 redesign has a fixed 60-EC first year; a 60-EC second year combining three compulsory 10-EC courses, the 10-EC Global Change IMPACT choice and four balanced 5-EC literature, linguistics and professional-English electives; and a 60-EC third year with a 30-EC minor, four further balanced electives and a 10-EC BA thesis. This route retains the generic degree’s broad literature, language and Anglophone-culture identity and is selected independently of UCR fit.

alternatives.label: English literature, language & culture
alternatives.concept: A balanced closest feasible English-studies curriculum combining literary analysis, rhetoric and stylistics, psycholinguistics, Anglophone and historical context, media, identity, qualitative research and advanced cultural interpretation.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum deliberately balances literature, language and cultural study, so the label names the three central elements rather than implying a dedicated English-language degree.
progression: Foundations in literary study, rhetoric, brain and behaviour, media, history and sociology precede advanced literary meaning, persuasive and creative communication, media, social theory and research. Introduction to Brain & Behavior precedes Psycholinguistics. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Literature, culture & media
alternatives.concept: A literature-led route combining close reading and literary theory with film, media, history, heritage, archaeology, gender, empire and cultural representation.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum centres literary study but substantially extends it through film, media, cultural history, heritage and art-historical interpretation.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the balanced closest match, this route removes psycholinguistics and most advanced rhetoric and social theory in favour of archaeology, gender history, media archaeology, empire, art, museums and heritage.
progression: Introductory literary, media, historical and material-culture study precedes advanced film and text, media and race, literary meaning, documentary, art, museum, heritage and disciplinary-writing seminars. All selected courses have no formal prerequisites and are offered in their assigned terms.

alternatives.label: Language, rhetoric & cognition
alternatives.concept: A language-centred route combining rhetoric, stylistics and communication with psycholinguistics, brain and behaviour, higher cognition, philosophy of mind and emotion, qualitative and advanced research, and social-cultural context.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum does not reproduce a formal English-linguistics major, but its strongest organising thread is language use and rhetoric supported by cognitive, philosophical and social inquiry.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the balanced and literature-media routes, this curriculum gives greater weight to psycholinguistics, cognition, rhetoric, persuasion, philosophy of mind and emotion, and advanced research while retaining a smaller literary-cultural foundation.
progression: Foundations in rhetoric, brain and behaviour, philosophy, literary study, media, history and sociology precede psycholinguistics, advanced communication, higher cognition, research, social theory and philosophy of emotion. Introduction to Brain & Behavior precedes Psycholinguistics, Higher Order Functions and Advanced Research Seminar. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.

candidates.label: English linguistics, language in society and cognition

routeSelection.route: Balanced literature, linguistics and global-culture elective route
routeSelection.basis: The generic target has extensive elective choice but no named specialisation. A balanced current route is instantiated by combining literature, linguistics, professional English and the broad Global Change IMPACT course, preserving the programme’s published identity more faithfully than a single-subfield route. The choice is independent of UCR fit.

selection.assessment: After the balanced closest match, two generator-backed and feasible directions remain materially distinct: literature, culture and media; and language, rhetoric and cognition. Both meet the pairwise distinctness threshold, so the maximum of three alternatives is reached.

blocks: Great Literary Works includes historically influential literature and provides the closest broad UCR counterpart to the dedicated medieval survey.
Both analyse how narratives construct personal and cultural identities.
Film & Text studies adaptation and transformation across literary and audiovisual forms.
Style & Meaning studies how linguistic choices produce meaning in social and textual contexts.
Psycholinguistics supplies the closest UCR study of cognitive language processing and development.
Rhetoric in Action develops argumentation, debate and applied rhetorical performance.
Persuasive Communication advances professional, audience-aware argument and presentation.
Creative Communication Laboratory examines meaning-making in communicative practice, while not replacing formal interactional linguistics.
Both examine how mediated stories shape social identities and cultural understanding.
Media & the Environment directly studies a major global-change issue through cultural representation and public debate.
Advanced Research Seminar develops independent evidence synthesis and research practice closest to the methodological side of a bachelor thesis, without claiming an English-specific dissertation.

notes.text: Groningen offers a dedicated English degree with sequenced English linguistics, English literary history, Professional English and a subject-specific thesis. UCR can construct related liberal-arts pathways from literature, communication, media, history, culture and cognition, but does not reproduce that dedicated sequence or guarantee the same depth in English linguistics and English literary history.
